Hobbit Standard Decks

Recent Standard decks from the creators you follow. Where we hold the list, its colors, price and wildcard cost are counted rather than guessed: 214 read their colors off the 60 cards, 0 off the creator's own title where no list was reachable. Every color starts on. Click a color to switch it off and every deck needing it leaves.

Every deck here runs at least one card new in The Hobbit, counted off its real decklist. Reprints do not count: matching on set membership alone once read 344 of 479 decks as Hobbit decks, every one of them on basic lands. The date on a card is the video's publish date, so a list edited after the video can run Hobbit cards under an earlier date.

It is not measured against your wildcard balance and nothing is hidden for costing too much: a deck needing 14 rares is not a worse deck, it is a deck that costs 14 rares, and more can be bought. How this was built. Channels resolved from your links, recent Standard videos pulled via the polite YouTube gate, then each video description parsed for the decklist link, the colors, the archetype, and whether it reads as a meta deck or a brew.

Where the price and wildcard numbers come from. Price is paper USD for the full list, summed from the cheapest Scryfall printing of every card, basic lands excluded, captured 2026-11-19. Paper prices move daily, so treat it as a snapshot for comparing decks against each other rather than a live quote. Wildcards are what MTGA would charge you after subtracting the 10,498 cards your collection export says you already own, bucketed by rarity. Both need the real 60-card list.

Buying a deck. Every deck carries a Card Kingdom button that opens their Deck Builder with the whole list already in the box. It is two presses from checkout, not a one-click cart: press Find Cards to price every line, then Add Items to Cart. Clicked through on 2026-08-25 and it reported Cards Selected 39/42, $274.91 on the first deck here. The button carries CK's own total when CK can fill every line; where it reads list instead, they are out of stock on at least one card, so the list still opens and the total is withheld rather than quoted short. The price above it is the cheaper of Card Kingdom and TCGplayer, and TCGplayer sits in the small print beside the local Kansas City option and the receipt.

Honest coverage: 215 of 215 decks carry real numbers. Four sources feed them: 119 pulled through a signed-in browser (113 Moxfield, 6 Aetherhub), 79 from lists the creator pasted straight into the video description, and 11 from MTGGoldfish, the one host that serves a machine-readable list without a login. Hover any price to see which source it came from.

Every deck on this page carries real numbers. The last 74 came through a signed-in browser pass on 2026-07-19, which reaches Moxfield and Aetherhub where an anonymous request gets a 403 from Cloudflare.
